channel.about_de:
Glück auf! Ich bin Horst – fast 40 Jahre Werkstatt, jetzt erkläre ich dir hier, was dir die Werkstatt meistens nicht sagt.

Auf diesem Kanal lernst du, wie dein Auto länger hält, wie du teure Reparaturen vermeidest und woran du eine ehrliche Werkstatt erkennst. Ehrlich, verständlich und ohne Fachchinesisch.

🔧 Auto-Tipps und alte Werkstatt-Tricks, die heute noch funktionieren
🛢️ Motor, Öl und Diesel: so hält dein Motor 300.000 km und mehr
❄️ Winter, Batterie und Reifen: gut durch die kalte Jahreszeit
⚙️ Automatik und DSG: die Fehler, die richtig teuer werden
🚗 Gebrauchtwagen: welche Autos halten – und welche du meiden solltest
🧾 Werkstatt-Wahrheit: Kostenvoranschlag, deine Rechte, typische Abzocke

Für Fahrer von VW, Mercedes, BMW, Opel, Audi, Skoda, Ford und Co. Neue Videos jede Woche – abonnier den Kanal, damit du keins verpasst.

Wichtig: Horst ist eine KI-generierte Figur. Stimme und Bild werden mit künstlicher Intelligenz erstellt. Die Inhalte werden sorgfältig recherchiert und mit Quellen wie ADAC, TÜV und Herstellerangaben abgeglichen. Sie ersetzen keine Prüfung durch eine Fachwerkstatt. Bei Bremsen, Lenkung, Reifen und Elektrik gilt: im Zweifel immer zum Profi.

channel.audience: German drivers aged 35–70 who drive used cars (VW, Mercedes, BMW, Opel, Ford, Skoda, Audi) and want to avoid expensive repairs.
channel.upload_rhythm: 3 videos per week for the first 4 weeks (see publishing_order), then at least 2 per week.

character.name: Horst
character.bio_en: Horst ran a small independent car workshop (freie Werkstatt) in Bochum, in the Ruhr area, for almost 40 years. Retired, he still spends his mornings in his workshop with his red 1972 Opel Kadett on the lift. Calm, direct, dry Ruhr humour. Explains what really wears out a car and what you can do yourself. Dislikes workshop rip-offs and 'miracle tricks' from the internet.
running_gags: His red 1972 Opel Kadett that always starts.
His wife Gisela, who drives an automatic and asks him questions.
His grandson Jonas, who wants an electric car.
never_claims: Never says he is a certified KFZ-Meister or that his workshop can be visited.
Never gives a fake address, fake customer reviews or fake certificates.
Customer stories are character stories: keep them plausible, never present them as verifiable facts or statistics.

fixed_lines_de.opening: Glück auf, ich bin Horst. Fast vierzig Jahre hab ich in meiner Werkstatt geschraubt – und heute erklär ich dir, was dir die Werkstatt meistens nicht sagt.
fixed_lines_de.signature: Ich sach dir das, wie’s ist.
fixed_lines_de.ending: Fahr vorsichtig, pass auf dein Auto auf – und wir sehen uns beim nächsten Mal in der Werkstatt.
fixed_lines_de.ai_label_on_screen: Horst ist eine KI-Figur. Inhalte recherchiert, kein Ersatz für die Fachwerkstatt.
fixed_lines_de.call_to_action: Schreib mir in die Kommentare, was für ein Auto du fährst – dann weiß ich, worüber ich als Nächstes rede.

voice.description: German man, about 65–70, deep slightly husky voice, calm pace, warm and direct. Standard German with a light Ruhr colour ('sach' instead of 'sag', an occasional 'wat'), never a caricature, always easy to understand.
voice.settings: Use the same voice ID for every video. Speaking rate ~130–140 words per minute. Generate audio per segment so each segment can be re-done alone.
pronunciation_notes: Write numbers as words when they are spoken in a special way: 'fünfhunderttausend Kilometer'.
Write abbreviations the way they are said: 'TÜV' (Tüff), 'ADAC' (A-De-A-Ze), 'DSG' (De-Es-Ge), 'DPF' → say 'Partikelfilter'.

reference_images.rule: Generate reference_main first. Use it as the reference image for every other Horst image so the face, clothes and workshop never change. 16:9, 1920×1080 or larger.
reference_images.reference_main: Photorealistic portrait of Horst, a 67-year-old German car mechanic, short gray hair, neat gray mustache, friendly lined face, light stubble, reading glasses pushed up on his head, wearing a dark navy work jacket (Blaumann) over a gray t-shirt, small faded embroidered name tag "Horst" on the chest. He sits on a sturdy wooden stool at a clean old workbench in a small, tidy German workshop, facing the camera directly, shoulders square to the lens, looking straight into the camera with a calm, trustworthy half smile, mouth slightly open as if about to speak. Background slightly out of focus: pegboard wall with hand tools, a vintage red Opel Kadett on a lift, metal shelves with oil cans, warm tungsten work lights, a small window with grey daylight. Medium close-up from mid-chest up, eye-level, 16:9, natural skin texture, documentary photography style, no text.
reference_images.variant_explain: Same man, same clothes, same workshop as the reference image. Horst holds a used spark plug between his fingers at chest height and shows it to the camera, eyes on the lens, explaining with a slight frown of concentration, mouth slightly open mid-sentence. Medium close-up, 16:9, photorealistic.
reference_images.variant_laugh: Same man, same clothes, same workshop as the reference image. Horst laughs naturally, head tilted slightly back, eyes still toward the camera, one hand resting on the workbench. Medium close-up, 16:9, photorealistic.
reference_images.variant_hood: Same man, same clothes as the reference image. Horst stands next to an open engine bay of a silver VW Golf in the same workshop, one hand resting on the fender, turned toward the camera and looking straight into the lens, calm expression, mouth slightly open as if speaking. Medium shot from the waist up, 16:9, photorealistic.
reference_images.negative_prompt: Negative: looking sideways, eyes off camera, profile view, extra fingers, distorted hands, text, logos, brand badges readable, dirty or messy face, second person in frame.
part_swap_list: car battery terminal with white corrosion

HORST_TALKS.what: Horst at the workbench, facing camera, talking (lip-synced). Main shot.
HORST_TALKS.use: Hook, transitions, each list item's first sentence, opinions, jokes, ending.

HORST_EXPLAINS.what: Horst holds a car part at chest height and shows it to the camera while talking (lip-synced).
HORST_EXPLAINS.use: When he names a part or a concrete gesture. Swap the part in the prompt (spark plug, oil filter, battery terminal, wiper blade, brake pad…).

HORST_AT_ENGINE.what: Horst standing next to an open engine bay, looking into the lens (lip-synced).
HORST_AT_ENGINE.use: Engine, oil, diesel and maintenance topics. Max 2–3 times per video.

HORST_LAUGHS.what: Horst laughs, no speech (2–3 s, image-to-video, no lip-sync).
HORST_LAUGHS.use: After a joke or a running gag (Kadett, Gisela, Jonas). Max 3 per video.

BROLL_STOCK.what: Real footage from royalty-free libraries (Pixabay, Pexels, Mixkit, Coverr).
BROLL_STOCK.use: Generic real-world scenes: traffic, winter roads, Autobahn, gas station, car wash, tire change, generic workshop, dashboard close-ups.

BROLL_AI.what: AI-generated image or 3–6 s image-to-video clip.
BROLL_AI.use: Precise mechanical close-ups stock does not have (sludge in an engine, corroded battery terminal, clogged DPF, DSG clutch), story scenes (Horst's old workshop in the 80s, a customer at the counter), anything with Horst's red 1972 Opel Kadett.

TEXT_CARD.what: Full-screen or overlay text made in the editor: item number (#7), a key figure (4 mm), a short rule.
TEXT_CARD.use: Start of each list item, important numbers, the 'Merke dir' summary. Never generate text with an AI image model.

shot_rules: Horst (any HORST_* shot) is on screen 25–35 % of the runtime; B-roll and text cards fill the rest.
One lip-synced avatar clip is never longer than 15 s. Longer Horst passages are split and alternated with B-roll.
Change the picture every 5–10 s (new B-roll clip, cut to Horst, text card). Never hold one stock clip longer than 8 s.
First 30 seconds: Horst on screen for the first sentence (hook), then fast B-roll showing the problem, then back to Horst for the promise.
Each list item: TEXT_CARD with the number → Horst says the item in one sentence → B-roll while he explains → Horst comes back for the tip or the punchline.
Cover any glitchy lip-sync moment with B-roll; the voice continues underneath.
Keep the AI label on screen for the first 5 seconds of every video.

video_structure.target_length: 14–20 min (≈1,900–2,700 spoken German words). Never under 10 min.

parts.content: Opening line of the reference title's promise in Horst's words, a concrete problem the viewer recognises (cost, breakdown, winter), and the promise of what he will show. Mention that number 1 / the last item is the most important (open loop).
Fixed opening line ('Glück auf, ich bin Horst…'), one sentence of credibility (40 years of workshop), one running-gag touch, then straight into item 1. No 'before we start, subscribe'.

Numbered items (5 to 25 depending on the title). Per item: what people do wrong → why it damages the car (simple mechanics) → what it costs in euros (with source or 'roughly') → what to do instead, step by step → a short Horst remark or story. Every 3–4 items: a mini re-hook ('Und Nummer 9 hat mir mal einen Motor gerettet…').
Short summary of the 3 most important points, safety reminder when relevant (brakes, steering, tires, electrics → workshop).
Call to action (comment your car), mention the Werkstatt-Handbuch only if the link exists, fixed ending line.

script_rules: Write in German, 'du' form, short spoken sentences (8–15 words). No bullet-point language in the voice text.

Start from the reference video (link in the video list): get its transcript, keep its structure and the kind of promise, never copy its sentences. Adapt to Germany (diesel, DSG, TÜV, road salt, Autobahn, euro prices, German brands) and add information it does not have.
Every number, price, law or technical claim goes into fact_check with a source (ADAC, TÜV, DEKRA, manufacturer, StVO). If no source is found, remove the claim or say 'ungefähr' / 'je nach Auto'.
Replace false or exaggerated words from the reference title: 'ILLEGAL', 'repairs 95 % of problems', 'forever', 'without any repair' → true versions ('ohne große Reparaturen', 'deutlich länger').
No medical, legal or financial advice beyond common facts. Legal points (StVO, Bußgeld) are stated as general information with the paragraph.
Safety: never explain work on brakes, steering, airbags, high-voltage EV systems or fuel lines as DIY. Say clearly: 'Das gehört in die Fachwerkstatt.'
Never accuse a named company or workshop chain. Describe practices and give the customer's rights (Kostenvoranschlag, alte Teile zurückverlangen, Rechnung prüfen).
Brands: talk about cars in general first. Name brands as examples, never as the main subject, except in the 'best and worst engines' format (about once every two weeks).
Use the running gags at most 2–3 times per video, short.
Use the fixed lines from character.fixed_lines_de exactly.
No idling advice: warming up a stationary engine is forbidden in Germany (StVO § 30) and bad for the engine.
Length check: count the words of all voice texts; 1,900–2,700 words.

broll.ai_image_prompt_en: Extreme close-up of a car dashboard at dawn in winter, the amber diesel glow plug warning light (coil symbol) lit, frost on the windshield edge, realistic European car interior, shallow depth of field, cinematic, photorealistic, no readable text, no logos, 16:9
broll.ai_motion_prompt_en: slow push-in, the amber light switches off after 3 seconds

decision: 1. Generic real scene (traffic, snow, gas station, car wash, Autobahn, parking, tire shop, someone driving) → BROLL_STOCK.
2. Precise mechanical detail, damage, inside of a part, or a scene stock does not have → BROLL_AI.
3. Anything with Horst, his workshop, his red Kadett, Gisela or Jonas → BROLL_AI using the reference images (keeps the same look).
4. A number, a rule, a law, a list title → TEXT_CARD (never ask an AI model to write text).
5. If a stock clip shows an American setting (US plates, pickups, US gas stations, US road signs, right-hand traffic signs in English) → reject it and search again or use AI.
broll_rules.german_look: European cars (VW, Opel, Mercedes, BMW, Ford, Skoda shapes, badges not readable), German/EU license plates blurred or not readable, German road signs, overcast northern-European light, Ruhr-area towns and workshops. No US cars, no pickup trucks, no US gas stations.
broll_rules.mix_target: Roughly 50–60 % stock, 25–35 % AI, 10–15 % text cards inside the B-roll time.
broll_rules.clip_length: Stock: cut 3–8 s pieces. AI video: 3–6 s clips generated from an AI image (image-to-video).
no_go: Readable brand logos or license plates
People's faces in close-up from stock if they could be mistaken for Horst's customers
Fake diagrams or text made by AI
Dangerous actions shown as normal (driving without seatbelt, working under a car on a jack only)

editing.subtitles: German subtitles from the script (SRT). Upload the SRT to YouTube; burned-in captions optional for the first 30 s only.
editing.music: Calm, low (−25 to −30 dB under the voice), royalty-free (YouTube Audio Library or a licensed library). No music under the first sentence.
editing.text_cards: Bold condensed font, white on dark navy (#1f4e79) or red (#b23a2a) like Horst's workshop; item numbers big (#7); max 6 words.
editing.sound: Light workshop sounds (wrench, engine start) on matching B-roll, low volume.
editing.chapters: One chapter per list item; first chapter at 0:00.

thumbnail.layout: Horst's face (left, ~40 %), looking at the camera, surprised or serious; the part or problem on the right; 2–4 big German words; one red arrow or circle.
thumbnail.prompt_en: Same man as the reference image, close-up, serious surprised expression, holding [PART] toward the camera, small German workshop background blurred, strong contrast, photorealistic, 16:9, empty space on the right for text, no text

production_pipeline: 1. Pick the next video from publishing_order (or the one the user asks for).
2. Inspiration: open the reference video, get its transcript, list its structure, its items and its promise. Note what is missing or wrong for Germany.
3. Research: build a fact sheet (claims + sources ADAC/TÜV/DEKRA/manufacturer/StVO).
4. Script: write the German script following video_structure and script_rules, output in script_output_schema.
5. Fact-check: every fact_check entry must be 'ok' or removed. Recount words (1,900–2,700).
6. Voice: generate audio per segment with the fixed voice; check pronunciation of numbers and abbreviations.
7. Avatar: for every HORST_* segment, lip-sync the segment audio on the right reference image (max 15 s per clip). HORST_LAUGHS = 2–3 s image-to-video without speech.
8. B-roll stock: search the queries, download, cut, log in credits.csv.
9. B-roll AI: generate the images, then 3–6 s clips; check hands, faces, wheels and logos.
10. Edit: lay the full voice track, place Horst clips and B-roll, text cards, AI label 0:00–0:05, music, sound, subtitles.
12. Publishing pack: title, description, chapters, tags, pinned comment, thumbnail; tick 'altered or synthetic content' in YouTube Studio.
qa_checklist: AI label visible 0:00–0:05 and in the description.
'Altered or synthetic content' ticked in YouTube Studio.
No avatar clip over 15 s; no lip-sync glitch left uncovered.
No American setting in B-roll; no readable logo or plate.
Every number has a source; no false word left from the reference title.
Safety sentence present when brakes, tires, steering or electrics are mentioned.
Length 14–20 min; chapters match the items.
credits.csv complete for all stock clips.
Impressum link in the description (required in Germany, § 5 DDG).
guardrails: EU AI Act Art. 50: AI-generated person must be disclosed (applies since 2 Aug 2026).
Impressum required in Germany (§ 5 DDG) before monetisation.
No fake credentials, no fake reviews, no invented statistics.
Do not use the face or voice of a real person for Horst.
If unsure about a fact, mark it 'to_verify' and ask the user instead of inventing.
title_rule: Take the title of a video that got many views and translate it word for word into German; change only the subject to bring it to Germany. Replace any false or exaggerated word with a true one. All 30 titles below already follow this rule.
